description: A small index of high-value safety contracts and the executable evidence that claims each one. It links to the normative rules and design documents instead of restating them. Maintained by .github/scripts/check_contracts.py; see docs/rules/safety-evidence.md.

models.exception: An API or I/O operation fails; cleanup and unwinding run.
models.process-death: The process or owner dies without graceful disposal; the OS cache, surviving processes and locks remain.
models.modeled-power-loss: A fault-model stream or device keeps only durable bytes: lost, torn or reordered unsynced writes.
models.device: An actual OS/VM reset or physical-device campaign; never inferred from a process-kill test.
models.corrupt-input: Damaged or unsupported persisted input is detected, diagnosed and not silently accepted.

contracts.title: Acknowledged durable transactions survive within the stated fault model

evidence.proves: Forced mapped leader/follower tickets and zero-frame/error/FOR UPDATE dependencies complete after unsupported sync without publishing a durable version; managed-flush/device failures stop the core, while exact payloads, indexes and sentinel survive saved OS-cache recovery and two cold reopens.
A forced final-release/cache-gate interleaving keeps Closed false while native admission still excludes Direct, then permits complete payload/index/sentinel verification after actual teardown.

Mapped cold/warm request-transform cycles, including reader-only disposal, release exact generation and facade/native participation with zero pinned-page finalizations; paused reaper proves registration survives until cursor disposal; peer write/checkpoint/cold reopen preserves complete payloads, index answers and sentinel.

The actual 100 ms process timer, another facade and its live cached stream do not retain a departed facade through AsyncLocal; no-ambient and already-suppressed controls preserve all peer payloads and final native release.

Cold/warm file-backed Shared callback targets owning their escaping reader collect with zero pinned-page finalizations; independent registry inspection proves lease release, and peer write/checkpoint/cold reopen preserves every payload, index answer and unrelated sentinel. Explicit-disposal and noncyclic controls remain covered.

Real public cache admissions overlap separately covered prefixes and failed later sync; lost/torn/reordered unacknowledged WAL bytes recover the acknowledged prefix twice with warm admissions and payload/index/sentinel oracles.

Unsupported grouped sync reports OS-cache-only durability, completes already-issued tickets, clears visibility/checkpoint pins and exposes every acknowledged payload through scans and primary/secondary indexes on three facades, after later writes, checkpoint and repeated saved-image/reopen recovery.

Short and completed second-frame append failures preserve the first successful frame using the updated batch extent; repeated file-backed recovery retains exact acknowledged payloads, indexes and unrelated data.

Plain/encrypted and checksummed/legacy writers match the frozen 256cfd0b9 WAL bytes across all 128 padding alignments, single/multiple frames, unconfirmed overwrite and truncation; enlarged buffers read exactly one frame and leave borrowed pages unchanged.

Engine-owned file batches mix real unconfirmed overwrites with a pinned-page append, preserve leased bytes and recover exact commit/rollback documents, indexes and unrelated data; writing after checkpoint re-reads the reset generation's extent.

Three independently owned Direct facades share two covered barriers; readers and acknowledgements advance by the captured prefix, either failed barrier poisons every facade, and repeated recovery preserves acknowledged payloads and indexes.

After a peer acknowledges and detaches, final close with checkpoint enabled or disabled fails pending writer and zero-frame tickets without acknowledging them or retrying the group; repeated recovery preserves acknowledged rows and exact indexes.

An uncertain I/O or non-I/O confirmation on a third facade poisons a captured or in-flight leader and a zero-frame waiter before teardown; no acknowledgement or later sync starts, the original cause reaches both waiters, and repeated recovery preserves complete payloads and indexes.

Plain/encrypted facade-owned transactions interleave foreign allocations with a peer header commit; owner commit or rollback, two reopens and subsequent allocations preserve complete payloads, indexed results and unrelated data.

Plain/encrypted killed Direct owners release native admission; two cold reopens retain acknowledged payloads and indexed results and exclude the uncommitted row, with runtime file locking enabled and disabled.
A failed WAL write stops attached facades and fresh attachment until final release, then cold recovery retains the earlier committed row and excludes both failed writes.

Plain/encrypted commit and rollback header publication tear a foreign empty image or confirming header and fail truncation; I/O and non-I/O faults stop later writes and both retained and disposed file images recover complete acknowledged payloads, indexes and page graphs twice.

A refused safepoint makes the transaction rollback-only; automatic rollback publishes foreign reservations, and subsequent commits and repeated reopen retain complete payloads, indexes and the free-page graph.

Plain/encrypted non-writable caller data with a retained file WAL publishes foreign reservations, preserves committed payloads/indexes through owner commit/rollback/abandonment and two unchanged read-only reopens, and materializes a complete page/free-list graph through repeated writable recovery.

After staging foreign reservation images, first/middle empty-page or confirming-header I/O failure refuses a pre-existing header-free commit and a later header publication without further writes; pre-cleanup crash prefixes and stopped files recover the prior acknowledged payloads, indexes and page/free-list graph twice.
I/O failures at the first/middle empty reservation and final header stop subsequent writes, preserve the prior acknowledged state and recover a complete page graph twice.
A is killed after B acknowledges a header commit; plain/encrypted extension, tail and free-page reservations recover complete payloads, selected secondary indexes and a complete reusable page graph.
Lost unsynced bytes and 15-byte tears at each physical publication boundary preserve the acknowledged state, atomic unknown commits and repeated recovery with independent page reachability.

I/O and non-I/O uncertain confirmations stop a captured or in-flight leader and a zero-frame dependency waiter before teardown, with no acknowledgements or subsequent writes/syncs; repeated file-backed recovery preserves seed payloads and exact indexes.

Failed leader padding/flush publishes terminal state and the causal write diagnostic under writer exclusion before queued admission; no device sync or subsequent commit succeeds and repeated recovery keeps complete rows/indexes.

No-op results, false Upsert, constraint errors and standalone FOR UPDATE cover observed pending dependencies; successful barrier images or the last durable image recover exact documents and indexes across checkpoint and repeated opens.
A dependency sync failure rejects results and errors, fails its predecessor and stops later engine calls; both automatic and explicit error paths are covered.

Retains each successful descriptor barrier image, then tears, loses and truncates every unsynced follower frame through GroupCommitRecovery; acknowledged rows and exact indexed contents survive read-only recovery and repeated checkpoint/reopen.

Held descriptor barriers with same/different-collection writers, partial checkpoint, exact reader prefixes and acknowledgement sets; either failed barrier stops all pending waiters before another sync.
Each operation's acknowledgment is recorded outside the engine; after a cut only the in-flight operation may resolve to old or new, and complete documents and FileStorage bytes are compared.
Sector tears of new WAL appends keep every acknowledged commit before them.
A rooted full checkpoint cut at each phase keeps complete payloads, secondary-index results and untouched data.
A failed checkpoint sync performs zero data writes and stops later writes instead of acknowledging them.
Device failures at the Shared commit barrier recover whole transactions and release writer ownership.
Child processes die at the reached hook; the parent requires the matching durable intent marker and verifies the recovered state.
Dirty-WAL recovery is interrupted again by transient and persistent read/write failures, then all acknowledged documents are compared and raw integrity is checked.
Two separately captured group tickets cannot publish beyond their covering sync while a later append remains pending (forced interleaving, without failure injection).

A retained live authority recovers a killed unsynced confirmation only after successful WAL and directory barriers; two failed recovery attempts retain the old visible version and recovery fences before two complete indexed recoveries.

gaps.text: No OS/VM reset or physical-device campaign: the device model is unclaimed.
Storage that cannot sync (#2242) is covered for its documented process-crash guarantee only; it makes no power-loss claim.

contracts.title: Recovery never combines incompatible data and WAL generations

evidence.proves: Forced mapped leader/follower tickets and zero-frame/error/FOR UPDATE dependencies complete after unsupported sync without publishing a durable version; managed-flush/device failures stop the core, while exact payloads, indexes and sentinel survive saved OS-cache recovery and two cold reopens.

All four native replacement stages retain admission across two plain/encrypted legacy Shared rebuilds; callback peer operations refuse, idle peers reopen current storage, and mutual writes preserve full indexed payloads and sentinel through two cold reopens.

Mapped explicit rebuild and live/cold upgrade/auto-rebuild refuse before replacement; data/WAL bytes, native identity and participant sharing remain intact, with complete indexed payload and sentinel verification after repeated reopen.

Unsupported grouped sync reports OS-cache-only durability, completes already-issued tickets, clears visibility/checkpoint pins and exposes every acknowledged payload through scans and primary/secondary indexes on three facades, after later writes, checkpoint and repeated saved-image/reopen recovery.

New plain/encrypted Direct/Shared databases preserve committed complete payloads and secondary-index results, exclude the rolled-back row, preserve an unrelated row, and leave data bytes unchanged through read-only reopen.
Final host close leaves recoverable complete outcome-unknown follower rows while preserving the acknowledged prefix and secondary indexes over two reopen/checkpoint cycles.
At three forced replacement boundaries, repeated child Direct/Shared admission refuses with identical file names and bytes; the owner and two indexed cold reopens preserve the committed row.
Direct/Shared child opens remain excluded after inode replacement; local compatible attachment reads the row and cold child admission succeeds only after final disposal.
Every reachable combination of install faults ends in the original pair, the complete replacement, or a guarded incomplete state (#2978).
Escape guard: the hit list of a successful rebuild equals the registered install faults, so a new fault point cannot be left out of the matrix.
A failed password rebuild restores the original data file together with its own WAL.
Repeated recovery failures keep Shared reuse and fresh opens blocked instead of admitting a stale original.
Header recovery interrupted again at each repair phase keeps the journal that selects the generation.
All backup and install gates are faulted while rebuilding indexes/FileStorage and changing passwords.

gaps.text: Directory-entry persistence of the rebuild marker and renames is not modeled (#3011); the install matrix is not power-loss evidence.

Forced final unregister waits for cache Gate while the table gate remains obtainable; caller-held reentrant gates cannot invert the admission order.

Legacy/mapped and writable/read-only native Shared claims admit a distinct Shared OFD without publishing the read-only Direct marker, exclude Direct, and preserve complete indexed payloads, rollback and sentinel bytes through two cold opens.
Read-only Direct excludes both Shared families/access modes; failed admission and final release permit both families sequentially without leaked locks or file changes.

Forced Unix marker-before-admission interleaving refuses both real NativeAdmission Shared family paths, then admits Direct and releases every native lock while retaining exact file bytes and indexed contents.

A completed core rebuild still under the real host maintenance lease refuses both same-thread and second-thread attachment; both variants fail at 45b85dc2e. After release both writers see each other's exact documents and two cold reopens preserve all acknowledged payloads, indexes and unrelated data.

Two actual facade rebuilds in plain/encrypted databases force attaches at all four native rekey steps and a second-thread attach while the facade still owns maintenance; canonical/symlink aliases refuse, unrelated files remain usable, completion exceptions release the lease, and exact acknowledged payloads/indexes survive two reopens.

Pauses read-only Direct after its marker but before admission; a distinct Shared descriptor must refuse, the reader then admits, and final release permits Shared admission with unchanged complete database bytes and payloads.

On macOS an unreadable sibling allows a mode-0444 data-inode fallback but refuses writable data; both preserve exact bytes and indexed/sentinel contents and release handles for later sibling admission.

Plain/encrypted mode-0444 data and mode-0555 directories (Windows ReadOnly attribute) reopen twice without byte changes, preserving exact indexed payloads, known rollback and unrelated sentinel data; Darwin first admission without a writable sibling uses the permission-fenced fallback.

Read-only Direct excludes distinct Direct/Shared processes with either access mode, survives unrelated descriptor close and non-final facade release, and admits a fresh process only after final release.
Both writable Direct and writable Shared refuse read-only Direct in another process, then allow exact indexed reopen after final release.

A paused final close retains same-file native exclusion while another file opens and commits; ordinary teardown and a reached data-page checkpoint fault both release admission and preserve exact indexed payloads and unrelated committed data through two recovery opens.
Direct and Shared native admission coexist with real managed read/write streams, remain held after unrelated stream closes, and release only with their last admission reference.
A child reaches a real indexed Shared write, a concurrent Shared peer reads and writes successfully, Direct remains refused, and the committed child/peer rows survive cold indexed reopen.
Every Direct facade reads only the durable group prefix through document scans and secondary indexes while followers from separate facades are pending.
Same-thread foreign facade work is refused, foreign Commit/Rollback cannot complete the owner transaction, rollback removes its row and a subsequent owner commit remains readable.
An admitted Shared reader returns all 256 rows after facade disposal and excludes child Direct admission until the reader closes.

Held descriptor barriers with same/different-collection writers, partial checkpoint, exact reader prefixes and acknowledgement sets; either failed barrier stops all pending waiters before another sync.
A WAL offset a reader resolved but has not read yet is never reclaimed under a concurrent checkpoint.
Long-lived cursors across partial checkpoints return exactly what an independent model predicts.
A blocked cleanup retains its detached resources while finalizers finish; the explicit test signal resumes disposal, and safety timeout expiry fails the test.
Independent abandoned cleanup workers contain reader and callback exceptions, free their roots and release ownership exactly once.

Rejected and throwing dispatch retain real abandoned cursor pins and leases, then the periodic timer retries and frees the GC root; peer write/checkpoint/reopen preserves full payloads, index answers and unrelated data.
A false submission result followed by retry and delayed original callback releases resources and frees the handle exactly once even when reader disposal or lease release throws.

Two real legacy Shared streams enter one cleanup batch; blocked or failing first-owner slot I/O cannot strand the other cursor and registration. Exact reopened payloads, indexed answers and a peer write survive.

Two real mapped warm streams enter one cleanup batch; a blocked cache gate retains exactly its own generation while the other participant releases its lease and completes final unmap. Live and disposed facades preserve pins, exact reopened payloads, indexes and unrelated sentinel data.
Held readers of interleaved Shared instances match an independent model.
Each attempt observes ready, fresh-owner update and re-pin, release and completion, so every handoff is a real one (#3033).
A read snapshot keeps its pinned version when its own transaction reuses a page ID another transaction freed and a safepoint marks it dirty, plain and encrypted (#3092).
A reclaimer killed mid-reclamation cannot invalidate another process's live reader or the reused-slot recovery.
Holds N and N+1 readers while two writers demonstrably complete, then overlaps checkpoint and slot reuse and checks all three versions.
Transaction admission overlaps checkpoints and readers under forced interleavings.
Cursor handoffs between threads overlap checkpoint admission and reclamation.
Ready, either envelope, ABI and capability damage refuse an already-open writer before DB/WAL mutation; accepted old snapshot payloads and cardinality survive.

gaps.text: Shared reader lease files have observer stages only; no registered fault point interrupts lease publication or expiry.

contracts.title: Supported historical inputs preserve their documented behavior

evidence.proves: Indexes written by the released 5.0.21 package survive migration power loss and a second interrupted recovery, with complete payloads and index plans.
The checksum cutover changes only the header; later writes migrate pages in any order.
An actual v9 predecessor creates vector/scalar indexes and clean/dirty WAL; the current engine migrates through every layer and v9 rejects the result.
Released 5.0.21 creates genuine old indexes; the current engine migrates them and the released reader refuses the promoted format.
Pinned actual v10/v11 predecessors reject newer fixtures without changing the data file or WAL.
The pinned actual v12 predecessor rejects v13 retained-WAL fixtures without changing either file.

Files written by the newest published prereleases and the latest stable package (plain/encrypted, clean/dirty WAL) are read or migrated with complete payloads and index results and stay writable, or are refused with both files byte-identical; each writer reports the package it loaded.
Plain/encrypted v4/v7 fixtures are upgraded with every publication phase interrupted and resumed, then extended with indexes, FileStorage, dirty WAL and read-only opens.

gaps.text: Fixtures lack provenance manifests (producer, recipe, hashes, expected outcome).

contracts.title: Query and mapping paths preserve meaning

evidence.proves: Forced mapped leader/follower tickets and zero-frame/error/FOR UPDATE dependencies complete after unsupported sync without publishing a durable version; managed-flush/device failures stop the core, while exact payloads, indexes and sentinel survive saved OS-cache recovery and two cold reopens.

Matching live transform delegates remain admissible, null/different delegates are refused, callback-bearing engines stay out of the process cache and all 160 rows invoke the original transform exactly once.

A retained participant does not keep its original transform delegate alive, but still refuses null or replacement transforms after that delegate collects; closing the participant permits a fresh opening.
Merged index ranges return exactly the unindexed results in both directions.
Generated queries compare indexed and unindexed plans against an independent model.
Cached and direct LINQ translation are compared concurrently, including rebinding.
Generated SQL statements are executed differentially against a full state model.
The first serialization is compared with an independently constructed BSON tree.

gaps.text: Cached and uncached paths share one translator; CLR evaluation is the independent oracle only where semantics align.

contracts.title: The safety machinery judges what it claims: oracles, markers, registries, corpus expectations, test settings and workflows

evidence.proves: A stalled operation fails its real child process with the replayable DEADLINE identity while another actor keeps completing operations.
Releasing the writer mutex while a protected core is still closing is latched and fails the ownership oracle.
A lost acknowledged write and a visible aborted write each fail the durability oracle on a cold reopen.
A swallowed or replaced injected fault fails against its declared disposition, while declared discard and failure lists pass.
Every smoke run feeds the core invariant families and the post-close, durability and fault-disposition oracles controlled bad states.
Unregistered markers fail statically, and a smoke campaign that never hits a marker its diff declares fails the Fuzz workflow.

gaps.text: A green self-test shows each oracle rejects one deliberately broken state, not that the oracle set is complete.
xUnit runs do not record reachability markers yet; markers reached only by tests are advisory.

Larger and smaller real remote requests retain the declared live stream/writer mapping without truncation.

Two preattached processes contend at the native turnstile; commit, rollback and killed owners hand off to 20-write successors, with two exact cold indexed payload/sentinel checks.
Repeated false Begin, implicit duplicate abort, failed retry registration and commit/rollback release to another process while the original owner remains alive.
Reuse-only death barriers assert no reset and actual marker reachability, repeat each death twice and preserve the same authority and complete indexed data through repeated protected recovery.
Matching header reuses; checksum, identity, valid alternate layout, process/generation capacity and requested size mismatches reset only at quiescence, then reuse without another reset.
Unknown ABI, untrusted namespace and inconsistent physical size repeatedly refuse before storage validation with byte-identical data/authority; restoring trusted bytes permits protected recovery.
An attached remote process fills the declared capacity; process/generation/size changes repeatedly refuse without mutation or validation, then succeed after owner death.

Ordinary Fact independently checks the product and attribute platform predicate, verifies two supported opens, or repeats unsupported platform/runtime refusal without changing database/WAL bytes or creating a mapping, followed by indexed cold validation.
GC finishes while cache Gate blocks abandoned-result cleanup; pins stay rooted until a normal thread releases the generation.
Disposal before or after record publication refuses admission and releases the participant only after the admitting call leaves the cache gate.
Each writer/recovery/failed-sync cut races a new public admission with two accepted warm generations; protected recovery preserves full old/current payloads and committed indexes.

A live scanner retains its local generation across death and physical process-slot reuse of children holding two warm generations; replacement changes incarnation and repeated recovery preserves current data.
All bootstrap/close hooks hit twice with preserved payload/index/unrelated collection checks before Ready.
Actual child death twice at every reached bootstrap/close boundary followed by protected validation.
All protected WAL offsets survive checkpoint with three mapped floors; clearing floors permits full checkpoint.
Malformed live record and Ready identity return unknown rather than omit a reader.

Plain/encrypted mapped facades retain one writer hold through repeated failed Begin and duplicate-key retries, reject peer callback self-waits, then permit a queued peer and preserve exact indexed payloads and unrelated data through two cold reopens.
A protected mapped core restores TIMEOUT from a real WAL; a concurrent exclusive lock contender times out before release, and owner rollback preserves indexed committed contents.

Both BeginTrans and getter-shaped writable opens recover partial tails under mapped WRITE. Unchanged adversarial regressions additionally check live attach, stopped close, authority damage and epoch saturation.

Two successor deaths at internal writer/open/structural publication boundaries retain the same live authority and accepted snapshot; exact indexed documents, unrelated data and mapped generations survive two repairs.
Terminal stops cannot publish or clear recovery fences; independent native probes establish release, and protected open restores complete known or outcome-unknown transactions.
Plain/encrypted rollback or killed allocation followed by new allocations/checkpoint passes independent page-graph, free-list, LastPageID and index-reachability oracles across two reopens.
A second facade uses the process cache with zero counted coordination operations under a peer-owned main mutex; idle cache owns no record.
Remote commit/checkpoint before and after record publication forces fallback before execution and returns complete current indexed payloads.
Skipping the final check reads a reclaimed WAL position and fails; correct admission reopens before executing.
Warm exact generations and full payloads survive each writer fence death and repeated protected recovery.
Expiry cannot retire an active generation; warm capacity fallback fails before query and releases main ownership.
Actual large WAL and independently large read page cache both prevent idle retention; sorter spill and expiry have separate resource tests.

gaps.text: Opt-in Linux x64 prototype only; Windows/macOS/ARM and actual device power loss unqualified. Writer publication has focused exception/process-death/prefix coverage; warm admission has focused fence/slot/recovery coverage; whole-path mapped power-loss fuzz and handoff remain later-slice gates.
